Industry · New Eden

Industry Management

Your pilots, their skills, jobs, planets, wallets and what they can build or fly.

Link EVE characters

  1. One-time setup. On developers.eveonline.com, create an application. Choose "Authentication & API Access", set this callback URL:
    Then tick below the permissions you added to that application. The login asks for exactly these; asking for one the application doesn't have makes EVE answer invalid_scope.
    Only the Client ID is needed. Never paste the secret key here.
  2. Log in. Pick the character in the EVE login window that opens. When you approve, the window closes by itself and the character is linked; its data syncs in the background, so you can log in the next character straight away.
    Log in with EVE Online
  3. Paste the return address. After you approve, the new tab lands on a page that won't load. Copy the full address from that tab's address bar and paste it here.
    To skip this step, open the tool with the launcher file instead of opening the HTML file directly. Logging in then completes by itself.

Skill check

Skill queues

What each pilot is training and when their queue runs out, from the last ESI sync. An empty or paused queue shows on the To-Do page unless you untick it here.

Key skills

Each line is a skill at the level you count as a requirement. Change a target with its dropdown. A green cell means that pilot meets it.

Planetary industry

Every colony on your linked pilots, ordered by when it will stop: an extractor expiring, or a factory running out of an input.

:A planet stopping more thanhours before that time shows on the day before, the last harvest it can wait for.

Who makes what

Each pilot's highest tier output, summed over their colonies.

Forecast

Today's value is your ISK (wallets, on the Misc tab) plus the stock value you enter. The forecast keeps today's ISK, stock and active contracts, adds the weekly profit of your planned activities and subtracts Omega renewals. One point is recorded per day to build your history.

Stock value

Enter a value by hand, or pick a kind of item (PI, moon materials, minerals…) to value it live from your hangars on the Stock tab: anywhere, in one location or in one hangar (e.g. only the hangar you sell from).

Planned activities

Expected profit per week. Untick an activity to leave it out of the forecast.

Objectives

Something you want to afford. It shows as a dot on the Total value line on the first day the total reaches its cost. The date is listed here even when it falls after the span shown on the chart (up to 10 years).

Omega costs

Each account with an Omega date on the Omega tab is renewed with PLEX on its expiry date, then again every period. Accounts already expired are left out.

Net worth

What you own, day by day: wallets, hangars, market orders, contracts and what industry jobs are making, for everyone or only the owners you pick.

Everything with a date in one place: industry jobs finishing, planets stopping, Omega ending, structure fuel running out, contracts expiring and objectives becoming affordable. Hover an entry for the details.

Time zones

    Omega status

    ESI doesn't share subscription dates, so enter when each account's Omega ends. Pilots with the same account name share one date. "Seen at last sync" comes from ESI: a pilot whose skills run below their trained levels is on Alpha.

    Paying for Omega

    The same settings as on the Overview tab: changing them here changes them there too.

    Calendar

    Assets

    What sits in your personal hangars and corporation hangar divisions, valued at the pricing you choose: Jita buy (highest buy order at Jita 4-4, the default), Jita sell (lowest sell order there), Jita split (halfway between) or one you add in Settings. Ore and ice are valued at the minerals they give when reprocessed at the yield set in Settings. Items inside containers in a hangar are counted. Ships' cargo and fittings are not.

    Where the value is

    Hangars

    Every location where each owner has items. Untick an owner or a location to leave it out of the totals, the chart and the forecast.

    Fittings

    Paste a fit to see which pilots can fly it with every module. In game, open the fitting window and use "Copy to clipboard"; the text it copies is the format this expects.

    Implants

    What each pilot has plugged in right now, by slot, read at each ESI sync (needs the Implants permission). Hover an implant for its name and bonuses.

    Pilots

    Job slots, industry bonuses and what each pilot can do.

    Roles

    Define a role from ships, fittings and skills, and see who can fill it. A role can need all of its requirements, or any one of them.

    Blueprint calculator

    What researching a blueprint's material efficiency (ME) further saves in materials, what the research costs, and how many runs pay it back.

    Jump freighters and Rorqual

    Who can fly each jump freighter, and the Rorqual (which can also jump cargo), from the skills the game requires for the hull. Each cell shows the training time, prerequisites included, from each pilot's attributes (~ means default attributes until the next ESI sync). Hover a cell for the skills.

    Jump fuel cost

    ISK per light year jumped, for each pilot who can fly a jump freighter or the Rorqual, cheapest first. Fuel use includes Jump Fuel Conservation (−10% per level) and the ship's own fuel bonus from the game data; range includes Jump Drive Calibration (+20% per level). ISK per m³ is the fuel for one light year divided by what the ship carries in its cargo hold and fleet hangar, with Expanded Cargohold II in every low slot and as many tech 1 capital cargo rigs as its calibration allows (jump freighters have no rig slots). Jump distances are in light years.

    Mining fleet

    Pilots who can fly the chosen barge or exhumer, roughly how much ore each mines per hour with the chosen strip miners and crystal (asteroid or moon), and how many ice blocks per hour with ice harvesters. Ships are assumed to fit Mining Laser Upgrade II (ore) or Ice Harvester Upgrade II (ice) in every low slot. Critical yields, mining boosts, implants and residue aren't counted.

    Ships and structures you can build

    Every ship and Upwell structure (citadels, engineering complexes, refineries…) with a manufacturing blueprint, checked against your whole roster: final build, every manufactured component, and invention for T2 hulls. Reactions, minerals and PI are not counted.

    Quotation

    What it costs to build something (materials at Jita sell or average prices, job fees and hauling) and the price to ask for the margin you want. Structures and hauling are set at the bottom of the Build planning page.

    Wallets

    All the ISK your pilots and corporation hold, and who holds it.

    Attribute boosters

    Every booster that adds to your attributes (cerebral accelerators): what it costs for each hour it runs and per extra skill point, and the best one for each attribute.

    Blueprint library

    The blueprints your pilots and corporations own, with their research levels: originals in research or copying and when they finish, the other originals, then every copy.

    In-game notifications

    Every linked pilot's notifications (Notifications permission), each one once with who received it.

    Your pilots' mining

    What your linked pilots mined anywhere (their own mining ledgers), over the period and valued the way picked here (the same settings as the Corporation page's Who mined what).

    Omega to renew

    Accounts whose Omega ends within 7 days (dates from the Omega tab).

    Structures to refuel

    Your corporation's structures whose fuel runs out within the warning set on the Corporation page.

    Skill queues to fill

    Pilots whose skill queue is empty or paused (from the last ESI sync). Pilots idle for more than 7 days only show when ticked. Untick a pilot on the Skills page to stop seeing them here.

    Empty job slots

    Manufacturing, science and reaction slots with no job in them, and finished jobs to deliver (they hold their slot until then), from the last ESI sync. Show picks the kinds of slot and the pilots listed; ✕ hides a kind of slot for one pilot.

    Ongoing contracts

    Client orders still missing goods (Contract management) and your contracts in game that are still open.

    Trips for a freight service

    Supply chain trips none of your ships can do (from the last plan on the Map page): contract them out, then mark them sent.

    Buy for reactions

    What the Reactions management plan still needs, after your stock: tick each line as you buy it.

    Buy for PI

    What the PI Management plan still needs for its days of stock, after your stock (its Shopping panel): tick each line as you buy it.

    Buy for builds

    Materials still to buy for the Planned and In progress builds of Orders management: tick each line as you buy it.

    Doctrine shortages

    Your fittings marked Doctrine (Fittings page), checked against a citadel's market: what nobody sells there.

    1 · Setup

    Your reaction slots, where you react and how you buy and sell. Slots and the Reactions skill come from your characters, stock from Assets, owned formulas from your blueprints, taxes and pricings from Settings.

    Composites and molecular-forged materials, by kind, with what one slot of each earns per cycle. Set how many instances of each to run.

    3 · Shopping

    4 · React

    The jobs to start each cycle and what you sell at its end.

    P4 planner · Settings

    For factory-only planets: you buy the P1 and P2, your planets make the P3 and the P4, you sell the P4. Prices come from ESI (Jita 4-4 orders, The Forge history).

    Pick production

    Which P4 pays best right now, per planet, and how many planets you give each.

    Shopping

    Every P1 and P2 the planets need for the days of stock you choose, minus what your hangars hold.

    Output

    What your planets make over the days of stock, and what it's worth.

    Planet batches

    What to drop off at one planet for the days of stock: load the hauler once, then fill planets one by one.

    Notes

    Your own notes, saved as you type. They stay in this browser when you replace the file with a new version, and they're included in backups.

    Profit and loss

    The ISK that really came in and went out of your wallets (pilots and corporation divisions), sorted by what it was for. Tell the page once what an item, a client or a kind of entry is for, and every entry follows.

    By month

    Profit of each activity, month by month (EVE time), over everything kept.

    Items

    What you bought and sold in the period (on the market, and in contracts sorted by what they held), by activity. Pick an item's activity once: all its purchases, sales, sales tax and contract shares follow.

    Who you dealt with

    Contracts, transfers and donations with other players and corporations. A client left on Automatic has each contract sorted by what it held (a contract holding PI and reaction materials is split between them); pick a client's activity to put all their contracts and payments there.

    Kinds of entry

    Every kind of wallet entry in the period, and where it goes when no entry, item or client choice applies.

    Entries

    Every entry of the period. Change one entry here when it shouldn't follow its item or client.

    Suppliers

    Import calculator

    Paste a list of items, pick where you need them and where you could buy them, and the hauling price. For each item it compares buying on the local market with buying at the other station and shipping it, walking through the sell orders for the quantity you need. The cheapest units are bought first, wherever they are: local orders, imported ones (with hauling) and, when ticked, your suppliers. Only what is for sale is counted.

    HaulingISK per m³ % of the value (collateral fee)

    Price comparison

    What a citadel sells, against another market's prices, for the items you pick: whole categories, or single items. Remove anything from the selection with its ✕.

    Market watch

    Tables that follow prices in a market for the categories, groups and items you pick. Each refresh is kept (one point per half hour, 60 days), so you see how prices moved since last time, over a day and over a week. Past prices aren't fetched: the 24 h and 7 days columns fill in as you refresh over time. Make one table per market, or several for one market.

    Arbitrage

    Items you could buy from the sell orders of a citadel, ship with a freight service, and sell instantly to the buy orders of another market at a profit, after hauling (ISK per m³ + collateral on what you paid) and sales tax. It walks both order books, so the units and profit are what the orders there can take right now.

    HaulingISK per m³% collateral m³ ISK per item

    Pilots and backup

    Add a pilot by hand (or use "Link EVE character" at the top), and save or restore everything this tool keeps.

    Pages

    Untick a page to hide its tab. Settings always stays visible.

    Pricings and HUBs

    Jita buy (JBV), Jita split and Jita sell (JSV) are always there. Add your own: a percentage of another pricing (for example 90% of JBV for a buyback), or a citadel's market (its lowest sell order, highest buy order, or halfway between; Jita is used for what it doesn't trade). Every price list in the tool offers them.

    % of

    Trade hubs

    The stations every market menu offers (Trading board, Import calculator, Market watch, Arbitrage, public contracts, broker fees…). The five main hubs are built in; add any other NPC station or player citadel. A citadel added here shows the orders it shares with its region (a public market); for a private market, use a citadel pricing above.

    Ore reprocessing

    The share of an ore's minerals you get when you reprocess it. Assets values ore and ice at the best possible yield, about 90.6% (Tatara with tech II rigs in null-sec, all skills at V, a 4% implant). Build planning reprocesses your own ore at your best refinery in the system where its minerals are used, by your best pilot for that ore.

    Market taxes

    Sales tax applies to every sale, instant sales to buy orders included: 7.5% base, 11% less per level of Accounting. Standings don't change it. The broker fee is paid on orders you place: in NPC stations 3% minus 0.3% per Broker Relations level, minus 0.03% × your faction standing and 0.02% × the station corporation standing (Connections and Diplomacy count), 1% at least; read with the Standings permission. Citadel owners set their own fee. An instant sale to a buy order pays no broker fee.

    Jump drive economizers

    Build planning hauling uses the best economizer found in your hangars; when there is none, it uses this one. The Prototype is the best but costs much more.

    EvE News channels

    What the EvE News panel on the Overview shows. Untick a channel to hide it, type over a name to rename it, move channels up or down (when two channels carry the same article, it shows under the higher one). Add any news feed (RSS, Atom or JSON) by its link; the tool reads it through the launcher.

    Time zones

    The clocks on the Overview, after EVE time. Rename a city by typing over it, move it up or down, or add any city by its time zone (e.g. Tokyo, or Asia/Tokyo).

    Characters

    Where each pilot's skill levels come from, and how fresh they are.

    Build planning

    Pick a blueprint and a quantity: the full build tree (components and reactions), what to buy, and who should run each job, given skills, free slots right now and each pilot's speed. Change a pilot in the table, or switch any component between build and buy.

    Structures and settings

    Where you build, the rigs fitted, how materials are moved and how blueprints and prices are counted. Shared with the Quotation page.

    Map of New Eden

    Known space with its stargates, coloured by security or sovereignty, in the real (3D, seen from above) layout or the game's 2D schematic map. Scroll to zoom, drag to move, click a system for details. Your citadels, stations with hangar stock, planet systems and homes are marked, and space held by the alliances you mark as allies is shown in dark blue. Pick a jump origin and a pilot's ship to see what's in jump range (high-sec systems can't be jumped into, so they're never highlighted).

    Homes

    Jump planner

    Jump-only route for the ship you pick: ships found in your pilots' hangars come first, then every jump-capable hull by class; ✓ means one of your pilots can fly it (the best of them is used, and a hull nobody flies yet is planned with every skill at V). It's the same choice as Range above, fewest jumps first (then fewest light years). With Citadels set to Prefer or Only, stops favour or require a structure the hull can dock in, from your corporation's citadels and the imported friendly ones: jump freighters and Black Ops dock anywhere, other capitals need a Fortizar, Keepstar or Sotiyo, supercarriers and titans a Keepstar. Midpoints are low-sec or null-sec systems of the kinds you tick; the destination can be any low-sec or null-sec system. Fatigue assumes you jump again as soon as each jump timer ends (untick "Any low/null" to limit the stops).

    Stop in min

    Gather items

    The shortest trip that stops in every system where your hangars (Assets) hold some of the items you pick, or that empties the stations you pick, from the system you start in. With a cargo hold, the ship goes back to the start to unload when it's full. Stops are numbered on the map.

    Security m³

    Supply chain

    Every move your planned builds, reactions and PI need, grouped into trips for your jump freighters and Rorquals: who flies what, from where, when each trip can start, and the routes on the map.

    Citadels

    Structures your pilots use, found through ESI: where your jobs run and where your hangars are (needs Structure names), your corporation's own structures with their fuel (needs a Station Manager and the Corporation structures permission), and any you find by name (needs the Find citadels by name permission). ESI has no list of every citadel you can dock in, so add others by name search or by hand.

    Import friendly structures from a list

    Copy a table of structures from a website (for example the EVE Jump Planner's structure list: select the rows, copy) or a spreadsheet, and paste it here. Each line needs the structure's name or system and its type; names like "1DQ1-A - Keepstar Name" give the system. They're shown on the map as friendly structures (◇) and can be used as jump stops, separate from your own citadels.

    Keep
    Import industry structures with their rigs

    Reads a structure list like the WC Structures sheet (columns system, structure, rig_1, rig_2, rig_3, structure_type, system_id, structure_id, tax). The structures show on the map as friendly structures (◇), and on Build planning you can pick one, or every one of a system, with its rigs and tax. If reading the sheet fails, open it, select every cell (Ctrl+A), copy, and paste here.
